title: What happens with AI
heading: What happens when every station gets AI
caption: In this thought experiment, faster work can make documents pile up where the work gets checked.

locator.title: The line
locator.label: Where the zoom sits: Review, between AI stations

pile: Illustrative queue: 28 documents in front of Review
out: No statistically significant company-level improvement observed
scope: Faros's observational 2025 report on software teams with high AI adoption. In its sample, no statistically significant company-level productivity improvement was found. <spent>DORA describes time moving from creating to checking</spent>; <inferred>the report does not establish that unclear specifications caused review load</inferred>. The 28-document queue is illustrative.

measured-the-load-moves-to-review.header: Measured: the load moves to review
measured-the-load-moves-to-review.description: In Faros's observational sample of software teams with high AI adoption, developers completed 21% more tasks and merged 98% more pull requests; review time rose 91% and pull requests grew 154%. The report found no statistically significant company-level productivity improvement in that sample [1]. These are sample findings, not a universal or causal prediction.

faros-ai-productivity-paradox-2025.title: Faros AI, The AI Productivity Paradox Report 2025 (23 July 2025)

engineers-say-the-same.description: Google engineers report that the time saved in creating is re-spent on auditing and verifying, and DORA reads this as work moving from authors to reviewers [1].

what-is-measured-and-what-is-inferred.header: What is measured and what is inferred
what-is-measured-and-what-is-inferred.description: The report observes more review time and larger pull requests in its sample; it does not establish that unclear specifications caused those changes. The findings are observational, vendor-reported software-team data, not a universal or causal prediction [1].

faros-ai-productivity-paradox-2025.title: Faros AI, The AI Productivity Paradox Report 2025 (23 July 2025)

every-station-faster.title: Every station faster
every-station-faster.script: Now imagine giving every station an AI assistant. In this thought experiment, some work gets faster, but a line can still bottleneck. Faros's 2025 report observed more tasks and pull requests, alongside more review time and larger pull requests, in its sample of software teams with high AI adoption. That does not prove unclear specifications caused the review load, or that every team will see the same pattern.

moving-bottleneck.title: Moving bottleneck
moving-bottleneck.script: When one part of a process speeds up, another part can become the bottleneck. In our example, that is the review station. The work has not vanished; the queue illustrates one way a bottleneck might shift. Whether that happens, and why, depends on the work and the team.
